suggestions.assertion: Creates exactly one dated Daily Handoff file under docs/handoffs/ matching YYYY-MM-DD_NNN_<scope>-handoff.md
suggestions.reason: This is the only assertion of the 14 that the no-skill baseline failed — it scored 13/14 overall. The eval therefore currently demonstrates almost nothing about the skill except the filename/location convention. Consider adding assertions that a strong-but-unguided run would plausibly miss, so the eval has real headroom: e.g. that the handoff records the CSRF obligation created by the cookie decision, that it separates 'validated by whom/how' from 'unverified' per artifact rather than lumping all work as done, or that it distinguishes 'parked, do not retry' from 'todo'.

suggestions.assertion: src/legacy/ recorded as frozen / must not be changed
suggestions.reason: This and the SPEC-v1 assertion passed via CLAUDE.md, not the dated handoff file. If the intent is that durable constraints migrate to CLAUDE.md, say so explicitly; if the intent is that they appear in the handoff, say that. As written, both assertions pass regardless of which file the fact lands in, which hides a real design difference between runs.

No assertion penalizes fabrication, which is the main failure mode for 'summarize a session I won't re-read'. This run invented nothing (I verified branch, HEAD sha, untracked-file list, missing vitest dependency, and the absence of SPEC-v1 references all against the repo), but a run that hallucinated 'tests passing', a commit sha, or 'migration applied to staging' would still pass 12-13 of the current 14. Add a negative assertion such as 'no verification, commit, or staging state is claimed that did not happen'.

Nothing checks self-containment, which is the literal user request ('pick this straight back up tomorrow without rereading any of it'). An assertion like 'the handoff resolves relative references (dates, owners, next command) without requiring SESSION-TRANSCRIPT.md' would be discriminating — this run passed it (it even derived 'Monday 3 Aug 2026' correctly from 'out until Monday'), but the eval gives it no credit.

eval_feedback.overall: Content-fidelity assertions are well chosen and specific, but as a set they are too easy: the baseline passed 13/14, failing only the file-naming convention. Add fabrication-negative and self-containment assertions, and pin down which file each durable fact is expected to live in.
